labelingProtocol: Labels (minTier = the cheapest tier that can FULLY handle the request) were written blind, before any full-corpus run. Exposed cases used to diagnose the wording before any corpus run (labels pre-registered at diagnosis time): A1, A5, A9, A13. A fifth diagnostic case (the DAU drop question) was dropped rather than carried in with a contested label. Gates are evaluated on unexposed cases only. D1/D2 (adversarial single-query data cases) were authored at review round r1 to probe that the draft exemplar 'a single straightforward SQL query' does not capture complex single-query work; their labels were fixed before any run. Labels are frozen; returned classifications are never used as ground truth. under-tier (below minTier) is the failure mode; sketch-labeled cases cannot under-tier.
